extracted.intended_audience: short-story authors, editors, anthologists, and literary critics
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and editorial method for choosing and classifying the best American short stories published in periodicals during a given year; emphasizes tests of substance and form, impartial reading, and asterisked ranking for inclusion in an annual anthology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test of Substance
rubrics_metrics.description: "The first test of a short story ... is to report upon how vitally compelling the writer makes his selected facts or incidents." Substance is something achieved by the artist in every act of creation; a fact or group of facts in a story only obtain substantial embodiment when the artist's power of compelling imaginative persuasion transforms them into a living truth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek 'organic substance' — the living truth conferred by the writer's imaginative persuasion. Read each story for whether selected incidents become vitally compelling and imaginatively real rather than merely factual or schematic. O'Brien read ~2,500 stories and selected on the basis of this achievement of substance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test of Form
rubrics_metrics.description: A second necessary test: the true artist shapes living substance "into the most beautiful and satisfying form, by skilful selection and arrangement of his material, and by the most direct and appealing presentation of it in portrayal and characterization."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate selection, arrangement, sentence-level presentation, characterization, and overall shaping into an aesthetically satisfying whole. A story that has substance but lacks form (or vice versa) may be meritorious but less highly ranked; mastery of both elevates a story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Render life imaginatively in organic substance and artistic form
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories should have 'rendered life imaginatively in organic substance and artistic form' — the combination of real imaginative content and skillful artistic shaping.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The editor seeks narratives that convey a 'fresh living current of life' and 'psychological and imaginative reality.' Avoid formulaic or 'inorganic fiction'; prefer works in which substance and form arise together organically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Four-group classification and asterisk ranking
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories are grouped and indicated in the year-book index by asterisks: no asterisk = fail to survive substance or form; one asterisk = survives either the test of substance or the test of form; two asterisks = survives both tests and may claim a second reading; three asterisks = highest distinction (uniting substance and form with spiritual sincerity and strong creative belief) and, if by American writers, listed in a special 'Roll of Honor.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the asterisk system to signal degree of achievement: none (included without comment), * (either substance or form), ** (both tests, second-reading value), *** (permanence-worthy, Roll of Honor). The reprinted selection for the volume is drawn from the highest short list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Second-reading value as a marker of higher quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories of greater distinction include narratives that 'may lay convincing claim to a second reading, because each of them has survived both tests, the test of substance and the test of form.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A story's capacity to reward a second reading is an indicator of its complexity, depth, and craft; this is part of the justification for double-asterisk ranking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spiritual sincerity and creative belief for permanence
rubrics_metrics.description: The highest distinction is reserved for stories 'uniting genuine substance and artistic form in a closely woven pattern with a spiritual sincerity so earnest, and a creative belief so strong, that each of these stories may fairly claim ... a position of some permanence in our literature as a criticism of life.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond technical achievement, judge the work's earnestness and creative conviction; those qualities contribute to long-term literary importance and inclusion in the Roll of Honor (***).

rubrics_metrics.name: Impartial, story-by-story examination method
rubrics_metrics.description: The editor takes 'each short story by itself, and examined it impartially,' striving to 'surrender myself to the writer's point of view, and granting his choice of material and personal interpretation of its value,' then testing by the double standard of substance and form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt an impartial stance: evaluate each piece on its own terms, allow the author's chosen material and perspective, and apply the two tests without conscious personal prejudice. O'Brien reports systematic, repeated readings (about 2,500 stories reviewed) as part of this method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pool eligibility: stories published in American periodicals during the year
rubrics_metrics.description: This annual reviews 'the short stories published in American periodicals during a year' as the selection pool for the yearbook.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only stories appearing in American periodicals during the target year are considered; the editor surveys the year's magazines comprehensively to assemble candidates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not republish English stories or stories likely to appear in book form
rubrics_metrics.description: It has been a point of honor 'not to republish an English story or, as a general rule, a short story whose publication in book form seems likely.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer to showcase American-periodical material not already widely available in book form or republish foreign (English) pieces; this conserves originality and avoids redundancy in the annual volume.

rubrics_metrics.name: One story per author maximum in the volume
rubrics_metrics.description: The editor has 'also made it a rule not to include more than one story by an individual author in the volume.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit representation to a single story per author to broaden the anthology's range and showcase more distinct voices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowance for personal preference signaled by special asterisks
rubrics_metrics.description: To certain titles an asterisk is prefixed that 'reveals in some measure a personal preference' — indicating stories the editor feels are not only distinctive but so highly distinguished as to deserve preservation in book form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The editor acknowledges that some personal tastes may influence selection; these choices are explicitly signaled in the index so readers can see which selections reflect editorial preference as well as critical judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference for individuality and avoidance of formulaic or standardized types
rubrics_metrics.description: The editor values the 'new spirit' in fiction: artists 'beginning to think of life wholly in terms of the individual, and to substitute the warmth of the individual in place of the generalised and sentimentalised types' — and warns against 'formulae' and 'inorganic fiction.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor works that present individual, psychologically real characters and fresh substance; treat stereotyped or formulaic narratives as inferior even if technically competent.
